title: What is a coronary artery calcium (CAC) score?
text: A coronary artery calcium (CAC) score comes from a non-contrast CT scan of the heart. It measures calcified plaque in the coronary arteries, usually reported as an Agatston score: 0 means no detectable calcium, and higher numbers mean more calcified plaque.

title: LDL cholesterol and atherosclerosis
text: High LDL cholesterol over many years contributes to atherosclerosis: plaque builds up in artery walls. Over time some plaque calcifies, which is what a CAC scan detects. So cholesterol is a cause, and calcium is a later sign of plaque that has already formed.

title: Using CAC scores to guide statin decisions
text: For adults at borderline or intermediate risk, a CAC score can help decide whether to start a statin. A score of 0 suggests lower near-term risk and may support delaying treatment; a score of 100 or more generally favours starting one. The decision is made with a clinician.

title: A high cholesterol number does not always mean a high CAC score
text: Two people with the same cholesterol level can have very different CAC scores, because plaque also depends on age, blood pressure, smoking, diabetes and genetics. CAC shows the plaque that is actually there, which is why it can refine a risk estimate based on cholesterol alone.

title: Calcium supplements and bone health
text: Calcium is essential for strong bones. Most adults can get enough from dairy, leafy greens and fortified foods. Talk to your doctor before taking supplements.

title: CT scanners: how they work
text: A CT scanner takes many X-ray images from different angles and combines them into cross-sectional slices. Radiation dose varies by type of scan.

title: Cholesterol-rich foods to watch
text: Egg yolks, organ meats and shellfish are higher in dietary cholesterol. For most people, saturated fat in the diet affects blood cholesterol more than dietary cholesterol does.

title: Familial hypercholesterolaemia
text: Familial hypercholesterolaemia is an inherited condition causing very high LDL from birth. People with it can develop plaque early, and guidelines typically recommend treatment based on the LDL level itself rather than waiting for a CAC score.

title: Can a CAC score go down with statins?
text: Statins lower LDL and stabilise plaque, but CAC scores often stay the same or even rise on treatment, because statins can make existing plaque more calcified. A rising score on a statin is not necessarily a sign the treatment is failing.

title: Calcium in coral reefs
text: Coral reefs are built from calcium carbonate. Ocean acidification makes it harder for corals to build their skeletons.

title: Limits of the CAC score
text: A CAC score only detects calcified plaque. Younger people can have soft, non-calcified plaque that a CAC scan misses, so a score of 0 does not rule out risk, especially in smokers or people with diabetes or very high LDL.

title: Heart scan prices compared
text: Prices for a heart CT scan vary by clinic and region. Some insurers cover the scan only when a doctor orders it.
